How long does 1-70 take in TBC Anniversary?

TBC Anniversary opened the Dark Portal on 5 February 2026 and runs the post-patch 2.3 curve, which cut levels 11-59 by up to about 18%. That makes 1-60 cheaper here - 3,379,400 XP - than on Classic Era, but the total to 70 is 10,141,700 XP because Outland is expensive: levels 60-70 are 6,762,300 XP, roughly 66.7% of the whole run.

1-70: hours to cap by play style, no XP bonus active
Play styleCasualAverageOptimized
Questing~90 h~54 h~34 h
Dungeon grinding~93 h~56 h~35 h
Mixed~86 h~51 h~32 h
PvP~217 h~130 h~81 h

Outland is still the fast half. Quest XP per hour from Hellfire Peninsula onward is several times what Azeroth pays, so the last ten levels take far less real time than their XP cost suggests. The usual plan is to push to 58, step through the Dark Portal, and never look back.

XP bonuses available

An XP bonus never changes how much XP a level costs - it changes how fast you earn it, so a +20% bonus cuts roughly 17% off the time rather than 20%. These are the bonuses that apply in this version.

XP bonuses in TBC Anniversary
BonusValue
Rested XP (typical play)+15%
Always rested (alt / short sessions)+30%
Joyous Journeys buff, if Blizzard enables it+50%

The two rested options describe the same buff at different intensities, so they never stack with each other - ticking one unticks the other. Everything else adds together. See how the numbers work for what sits behind the XP/hour rates.

Frequently asked questions

How long does 1-70 take in TBC Anniversary?

1-70 is 10,141,700 XP, and Outland from 60 to 70 is 6,762,300 of that, about 66.7%. Questing with no XP bonus lands near 90 hours casual, 54 hours average and 34 hours optimized, because Outland quest XP per hour is several times higher than Azeroth's.

How much XP is 1-60 in TBC Anniversary?

3,379,400 XP, against 4,084,700 XP on Classic Era. The post-2.3 curve cut levels 11-59 by up to about 18%, so the Azeroth half of a TBC run is meaningfully shorter than the same levels on a Classic Era realm.

When should I go to Outland?

At 58, as soon as the Dark Portal lets you through. Hellfire Peninsula quest rewards and XP outclass anything left in Azeroth at that level, and levels 58-60 are only 337,800 XP, so there is little reason to finish Azeroth zones first.

Is dungeon grinding worth it in TBC?

It is close. Dungeons come out around 56 hours at an average pace against 54 hours questing, so the choice is mostly preference. Mixing the two is fastest at roughly 51 hours, since Outland dungeon quests pay well alongside a normal questing route.
